days.blurb: Device pairing with Mac or PC via USB requires explicit user trust confirmation on the iOS or iPadOS device, after which a 2048-bit RSA pairing record is exchanged and stored. This record enables the host to initiate backup, sync, and diagnostic connections. Accessories connecting via Lightning or USB-C have restricted data access until the device has been unlocked at least once. USB Restricted Mode limits USB accessory communication with the device if it has been more than an hour since the device was last unlocked, protecting against forensic tools and exploit devices connected to a locked iPhone.

Apple applies data minimization and privacy-by-design principles across its platforms to protect users' personal data. Sensitive processing – such as face recognition in Photos, health trend analysis, and on-device Siri – is performed locally using the Neural Engine rather than uploaded to servers. When aggregate statistics must be collected, Apple uses differential privacy techniques injecting calibrated mathematical noise to prevent identification of individuals. Data in transit is protected by TLS; data at rest is encrypted with keys Apple does not hold for end-to-end encrypted services, ensuring Apple cannot access personal content even under legal compulsion.
days.section: How Apple protects users' personal data

days.blurb: Ultra Wideband radio on Apple devices enables centimeter-precise spatial ranging for passive car key entry, Find My precision finding, and directional AirDrop. UWB ranging sessions are protected by session keys derived from a prior Bluetooth pairing exchange, ensuring only previously authenticated devices can establish ranging sessions. The short range of UWB combined with physical-layer time-of-flight measurement makes relay attacks significantly harder than with Bluetooth or NFC. Car key UWB ranging uses enhanced ranging calibration data and cryptographic binding of measurements to prevent spoofing of distance values by a relay adversary.

Apple Configurator for Mac enables administrators to configure, supervise, and restore iPad, iPhone, and Apple TV devices in bulk over USB without internet access on the target devices. For Mac and Apple Vision Pro restore operations, the required OS update files are downloaded from Apple servers over TLS and installed directly, with the file deleted after use to prevent unauthorized re-use. Devices enrolled via Apple Configurator can be added to Apple School Manager or Apple Business Manager, gaining supervised status and mandatory device management enrollment while still enforcing Activation Lock requirements that apply during normal nontethered activation.

The Notes app protects individual notes using per-note encryption keyed to a user-set password hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512. The derived key is stored in the iOS Keychain with Data Protection Class A (CompleteWhenLocked), so locked notes cannot be accessed without device unlock plus the Notes password or biometric authentication. Shared notes enforce iCloud-based access control so only invited collaborators can view or edit content. Note content and attachments are encrypted at rest, with only ciphertext stored in the underlying database, preventing unauthorized access even if the SQLite database file is extracted from a device backup.
days.section: Secure features in the Notes app

days.blurb: Apple platforms support TLS 1.2 and 1.3 with forward-secrecy cipher suites mandated by App Transport Security. Preferred cipher suites include ECDHE with AES-256-GCM, AES-128-GCM, and ChaCha20-Poly1305, with SHA-2 family hash functions for integrity. SSLv3, RC4, and 3DES are explicitly disabled. Certificate validation includes full chain verification to trusted roots, OCSP stapling for revocation checking, and Certificate Transparency enforcement requiring signed certificate timestamps from qualified CT logs. ATS additionally requires a minimum RSA key size of 2048 bits or ECC keys of at least 256 bits, blocking weak legacy configurations.

Background Security Improvements enable Apple to ship rapid security remediations – including XProtect signature updates, runtime mitigations, and new security policies – independently of full OS releases. The mechanism uses cryptographically signed disk images called cryptexes (Cryptographic Extensions), which are verified and mounted at boot alongside the main system volume. Cryptexes carry their own Sealed System Volume hash tree guarantees and are delivered via standard software update infrastructure without requiring a full OS upgrade, allowing Apple to address newly discovered vulnerabilities with minimal user friction.

Apple's Encryption and Data Protection framework provides hardware-accelerated AES-256 encryption for all data stored on devices. Every file on NAND storage is encrypted using a unique per-file key, which is itself wrapped by a class key derived from the device UID and – for sensitive classes – the user's passcode. This key hierarchy, maintained in keybags, enables instantaneous crypto-erase by discarding the media key, and protects data when the device is locked by making class keys unavailable without passcode or biometric authentication. The Secure Enclave manages the entire key hierarchy, ensuring the OS and apps cannot access raw cryptographic material.
